reuse.why: Extends the existing shared getScheduledAmount and computes the tolerance with the existing getApproxNumberThreshold used by rule matching, so the 7.5%/cent rounding is not re-derived.

duplication.why: No logic is copied; the only redundancy is schedule-template's own op ternary, which now repeats the op dispatch the shared function performs.

placement.why: The worst-case rule stays in shared/schedules.ts and each caller just passes its operator.

scope.why: Only the shared rule, its callers and the forecast raw type are touched.

maintainability.why: One definition of the rule, but the new op argument sits after a boolean so every caller passes a bare `false`, and the template still gates which ops reach the function.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All amount sites call getScheduledAmount; tolerance comes from getApproxNumberThreshold.

disguised_duplication.where: None; the template's `op === 'isbetween' || op === 'isapprox'` guard is redundant gating, not a copy of the rule.

one_place.where: The approximate rule lives in shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount, but server/budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList still decides which operators get the worst-case treatment with its own ternary that had to be extended to 'isapprox'
